lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON.

instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Write a draft script for each of my product's capabilities in each video format I picked: the format's own lines filled with the capability's words, the word count of every line against the format's measured budget, the shots, the filming notes, and every fact still missing listed with what would fill it", and give it nothing more: every input is optional.
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:generate-fill-scripts-for-formats and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Takes one request: formats (each with its template: lines with a measured word budget and seconds, slots with their pictures, shoot and reuse notes, an optional note, and which words count: all words, or only quoted on-screen words), capabilities (the person's own words for each, any fields), the saved catalog listing of each capability (title, job, steps), the page layout, and optionally an index page.
4. It reads and writes only its own rows through the records door: record:setting (records:read).

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
